answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, identities lock their own refundable smart-contract bonds, making multiple identities costly. Slash transactions only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task. This approach ensures a secure summit, where only genuine participants can access resources, preventing malicious actors from exploiting the system like a velvet-wrapped wolf. As the system operates, it will force attackers to wander, exposing their true intentions, and ultimately leading to a more secure and trustworthy network.
